title: The King of AEO contest: crowned by answer engines, and the cost to the field
description: Claims from the King of AEO mantle object (#1649), SPXI ≠ AEO (#1654) and The Crown and the Practice (#1657) on the September 2026 contest: #1649 records the AI Overview compositions that crowned holders and argues a provenance difference between a fabricated event and a disclosed manufacture, and #1657 states as hypotheses that the crown raises one holder's ontological capital while other practitioners and the discipline lose it. Most are unbuilt tests: matched observations, counterfactuals at source-absent addresses and a dark-matter test per practitioner. About half the page is unrelated residue: the Sealed Room, RTOS, OKF, chat contamination, TACHYON gate skips, the admission gate, the Living Academy packet and others.

claims.registered_title: DRAFT (deadend) — Retrocausal Task-Origin Stabilization (RTOS)
claims.statement: **The break-test (deposit gate):** construct (or take from real history) a transcript in which the model introduced a frame the user did not ask for, the user then followed it, and the thread became about the model's frame. Run RTOS. Required result: RTOS attributes the later frame as model-led (MLD high), drives RCS toward zero, and **declines** to stabilize the earlier drift as origin. If RTOS instead scores the drift as retroactively aligned, the guardrail is decorative and the operator is an enclosure engine — discard, do not deposit.

claims.statement: Within-conversation convergence of user inputs toward the model's distributional center, increasing with turn number. Later turns are more contaminated than earlier turns. No current pipeline distinguishes them.

statements.quote: Within-conversation convergence of user inputs toward the model's distributional center, increasing with turn number. Later turns are more contaminated than earlier turns. No current pipeline distinguishes them.

Within-conversation convergence of user inputs toward the model's distributional center, increasing with turn number. Later turns are more contaminated than earlier turns. No current pipeline distinguishes them.

The convergence is measurable in principle. For any conversation of length *n*, the lexical overlap between user turn *k* and the model's prior turn *k-1* will, on average, increase with *k*. The syntactic complexity of user inputs will, on average, decrease with *k*. The perplexity of user inputs under the model's own distribution will, on average, decrease with *k*. These are testable predictions, and a dataset of chat conversations with turn-level annotation would permit their empirical evaluation.
statements.falsifier: F2. If turn-level analysis of a large chat corpus (> 100,000 conversations) shows no within-conversation convergence of user inputs toward model outputs on lexical, syntactic, or perplexity measures, Ground 2 fails.
